newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases vs dlr, investors cautious.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases vs dlr, investors cautious.

text.p: The Kenya shilling continued to ease against the dollar as markets remained cautious, commercial dealers said on Friday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean commercial rate of 59.17 against the dollar compared to 59.11 on Thursday, while against sterling the shilling was posted at a mean of 98.90 from 99.15.
"There's a lot of demand for dollars, investors are disinvesting from the local treasury bill market," said one dealer.
Another dealer said: "They would rather place their money into deposits with shorter tenures, rather than hold them for 91 days."
They said that after last week's political unrest which triggered panic buying of dollars and weakened the Kenyan shilling, foreign investors were still wary of this emerging market.
"It was pretty obvious after the riots on Monday last week but now it's more sustained. They (foreign investors) are still getting out (of the market)," said a forex dealer.
A lull in the coffee market has reduced inflows of dollars and put pressure on the Kenyan shilling following the suspension of coffee auctions for two weeks, a dealer said.
Coffee is Kenya's second largest foreign exchange earner after tourism. The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at between 5-11 percent from Thursday's 11-14 percent.
